title: Egg, yolk only, cooked, NS as to fat

content.title: About
content.content: The cooked egg yolk is the nutrient‑dense part of the egg, containing most of its fats, vitamins, and minerals. When boiled, the yolk firms up but retains the majority of its nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The yolk holds almost all of the egg’s nutrients, including vitamins A, D, E, K and the B‑complex.
Cooked yolk is easier to digest than raw yolk.
Although yolk is a source of cholesterol, current research shows moderate intake does not raise blood cholesterol for most people.
Yolk contains lecithin – a natural emulsifier beneficial for liver and brain health.
Boiling preserves nearly all of the yolk’s antioxidants.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and promotes bone health.

items.title: Contains lecithin
items.content: Lecithin helps liver function and supports normal nervous system activity.

items.title: High in biotin
items.content: Biotin (vitamin B7) is important for carbohydrate, fat, and protein metabolism.

items.title: Provides iron and selenium
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and antioxidant protection.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: Consuming large amounts of yolk may raise cholesterol levels in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to egg whites or yolks.

items.title: Excess vitamin A
items.content: Overconsumption can lead to vitamin A toxicity, especially in pregnant women.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked yolk can be eaten on its own, added to salads, pâtés, sauces, or used as a filling for sandwiches. It can also be mashed and mixed with vegetables for a nutrient‑rich snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled yolks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if any off‑odor or discoloration develops.
